_comment: Single source of truth for every scheduling decision. The engine is dumb; the rules live here. Changing a rule is an edit to this file, never a rebuild. Audited by Spencer 2026-08-09.
_status: SIGNED OFF by Spencer 2026-08-21. Supersedes 2026-08-09-v1 (DRAFT). Three open questions closed by Spencer this session (new-customer day, review horizon, Federal Way). One remains and is a MEASUREMENT, not a decision: cadence field fill rate, answered by Phase 0. This file wins over any prose rule in CLAUDE.local.md, a script comment, or a memory note; where they disagree, the loser gets corrected rather than left standing.

product._comment: Product comes from the job's LINE ITEM, never jobType. All jobs are 'Recurring' in Jobber, so jobType tells you nothing. Match case-insensitively; scan ALL line items (Repeat Customer Discount appears as a second item). Mixed dashes are present in real data.

matchers._note: treat as TMCP unless told otherwise
treat as TMCP unless told otherwise

activity._comment: Activity is BINARY. The level (L/A, M/A, H/A) is irrelevant - only activity vs none. Supersedes the 2026-07-26 graded ladder entirely.
countsAsActivity: a miss on a trap (hit but did not hold - a mole was working and got away)
doesNotCountAsActivity: old mounds - dried, crusted, grass growing through. A yard covered in old sign can still be a true N/A.

sourceFields._comment: report-sync.mjs writes these Jobber job custom fields. The old engine parsed them and then ignored them, reading only free-text Next Action - which is why a miss only shortened the interval when a tech happened to type it there.
sourceFields.fallbackPolicy: If structured fields are empty, fall back to free text AND report the gap per tech. Never silent.

cadence._comment: Intervals are expressed in WEEKS, never days, so a customer never walks off their weekday. Monthly is the Nth weekday of the month (12 visits/year, weekday held), NOT 28 or 30 days.

onCatch._note: A catch overrides the activity code. Caught >=1 mole means the property is not quiet, even if the note reads L/A or N/A.

quiet._note: e.g. always the 2nd Tuesday. Weekday holds, 12 visits/year, interval flexes 28-35 days.

QUICK_FIX._comment: A 5-week weekly series. Every visit is ~7 days apart regardless of activity code or catch - weekly by construction.

seriesExhaustedWithActivity._note: When the 5 weeks are used up and activity remains, it is a HUMAN sales decision: add one more visit, or sell a TMCP or another month. The engine flags, never books.

application._comment: How an interim visit gets added.
application._whyNot: Moving the recurring visit forward just relocates the gap downstream - Avila 7/30 would have left 7/30->9/17 = 49 days.
application.addOnlyWhen: The job's first open future visit is LATER than (lastVisit + requiredInterval). If an existing visit already falls inside the interval, do nothing.
application.targetDate: The territory grid day inside the required week.

dayOfWeek._comment: Consistency is an EMERGENT property of the territory grid, never a per-job pin. The grid assigns a weekday to geography; a job inherits its day from where the property is. Pinning individual jobs is what fought Spencer in iterations 1 and 2.
dayOfWeek.preference: Jobs should repeat on the same weekday wherever possible.
dayOfWeek._spencer: If it means the routes are no longer tight and a visit must get shifted to a new day, that is OK.
dayOfWeek.recovery: A displaced visit settles back onto the grid day next cycle, because the geography has not moved.

noWeekends._comment: Got Moles is Mon-Fri. Any Saturday or Sunday visit is a defect to fix, never to route.

newCustomerFirstVisit._visit1Why: The first visit is a human decision made at intake and is out of scope for the engine. Whatever day the office sold is the day that is honoured — moving it would break a promise already made to the customer.
newCustomerFirstVisit._fromVisit2Why: Spencer: a new customer should settle into its rightful day on visit 2. So the sold day is honoured once and never becomes a permanent pin — otherwise every new customer is a standing exception to the grid and the neighbourhood grouping erodes one sale at a time.
newCustomerFirstVisit._implementation: Treat visit 1 as fixed. From visit 2 the job inherits the route-day of its geography like any other job, with no per-job pin recorded.

territory._comment: Ownership is DERIVED on every run from address + date. Never stored, never carried forward - that is what stranded 11 visits on Tavis across the 08-17 handover.

geoSplitLines._comment: Three boundaries cut THROUGH zip codes and cannot be expressed as a zip list. Resolved per ADDRESS from real coordinates. Coordinates come from OptimoRoute - Jobber returns no lat/lng.

thurston-i5-101._note: Olympia north of I-5/US-101 day one, south day two. 98501/98502/98503/98513 all straddle it.

bellevue-ne8th._note: T1/T2 line runs north to NE 8th St; 98004 straddles it. Still changes OWNER — Alias north, Tavis south from 2026-08-17.

sr-516._note: NOT a constant. Before 2026-08-17 this line changed the OWNER (Cory north / Robert south). From 2026-08-17 the handover gives Robert both sides, so it changes only the DAY. Derive with crossesOwners(T, line, date) in geo-side.mjs — never store the answer. The stored crossesOwners flag was deleted 2026-08-21 (defect D3) after it drifted from the handover table.

territory.handovers: Applied by date automatically. A visit pulled forward across a handover line re-derives its owner rather than keeping the old assignee.

assignment._comment: Two layers, only one of them drawn. Territory (highway-bounded) answers WHICH TECH and changes only when hiring. Route-day answers WHICH WEEKDAY and is never drawn - it emerges from sticky per-job assignment. Spencer 2026-08-11: hand-drawn sections have to be constantly refined as density changes, which is the six territory re-cuts.
assignment._atomDef: One tech, one weekday, ~8 hours. A tech is five route-days.

firstVisit._comment: OUT OF SCOPE. The quote must be approved before the job exists, so the office books visit 1 by hand at intake. Spencer 2026-08-11: 'I'm manually adding a day when these people are reaching out.' This works and is not being automated.
firstVisit.inScope: Every visit AFTER the first. 'The reschedule of the second, third, fourth, fifth, whatever visits is what needs to be addressed.'

placement._comment: Spencer 2026-08-11: 'They should fall into their exact category. If they need to get pushed out a week to fall on the right day, then that is fine.' No cleverness about squeezing a customer onto a wrong day.
steps: Resolve the property's section from geography (territory + geoSplitLines).
Book the first occurrence of that weekday that satisfies the cadence interval.
If that pushes the visit out by up to a week, that is acceptable.
placement._why: Predictable, explainable to a customer, and verifiable by eye - which matters because Cory takes this over.

stickiness.mayPropose: Small nudges (~10 jobs) for Spencer to approve when they meaningfully tighten a route.

assignment.sectionsAreAView: Territory sections are what you see when the board is coloured by assignment. The map is an OUTPUT, never an input.

duration._comment: Every capacity number depends on this and nothing currently models it. OptimoRoute plans with ONE uniform service duration for every stop and every tech. Spencer 2026-08-11: bigger properties DO take meaningfully longer - scale by acreage, matching the pricing tiers.
duration._tiersUnset: Values to be derived in Phase 0 from completion timestamps joined to property acreage. Do not guess them.
duration.setVsCheck: First visit (set) is longer than a routine check. Old brief used 10 min check / 20 min set - unvalidated.

perTechRates._comment: Spencer 2026-08-10: 'not yet, we don't have enough data on the new guys.' Measured medians min/stop: Cory 17.3, Robert 17.7, Luke 19.1, Alias 21.3, all-tech 17.8 - a 23% spread. But Robert had only 89 stops and Tavis none, so pinning a rate that thin bakes a learning curve into every future route. Metric also blends drive with on-site time, so spread ground is penalised.
perTechRates.revisitWhen: Robert and Tavis each have ~15 field days / 300+ stops. Re-run tech-pace.mjs. Apply only beyond any week whose customers already hold arrival windows.

capacity._targetNote: Revised down from 9h normal / 10h ceiling on 2026-08-11. Spencer: 'if that means that I have to hire more people, then I have to hire more people.'

overflow._comment: A customer is never turned away, never made to wait, and never moved across a territory line to protect the 8h target. The day runs long instead.
overflow._whyMeter: Overflow is silent. Every individual decision is right and the day drifts to 9.4h with nobody deciding it - which is how T1 reached 40.7h. Record every event: date, tech, route-day, minutes over, causing customer.
overflow.meterIsTheHiringSignal: e.g. 'T1 Tuesday has exceeded 8h for six straight weeks, averaging 9.4h, absorbing 23 new customers since June.'

staffing._comment: Staff so busy season still fits inside 8h days, carrying slack in quiet months. Requires the seasonal swing, which is unmeasured - Phase 0.
staffing._seasonality: A quiet TMCP customer is monthly; one catch later the same customer is weekly. That is 4x the route capacity with no new sale and no change in geography. A route-day that fits in October can be 2-3x over in spring.

capacity.hiringCreatesRouteDays: Hiring does not re-cut territories. It creates five new route-days seeded from the outer edges of the fullest existing ones, so only marginal customers move.
capacity._why: Drive-min per stop ranges 4.5 (Burien) to 18 (peninsula), so 111 visits can outweigh 146. Comparing visit counts led to a proposal to move Federal Way off Robert when Luke was actually the heavier tech.

spencerFieldWork._comment: Spencer does minimal field work - peninsula Tuesday only. Never assign him route stops to absorb overflow.

priority._comment: What wins when these conflict. Ordered, highest first.

order._note: Never move a visit the customer has already been told about.
Spencer's call 2026-08-09: tight routes and sane hours win over both cadence timing and weekday consistency.

emailFreeze._comment: Jobber emails arrival windows at ~14:00 PT the day before. A date locks at 14:00 on D-1. Today is never writable.

approvalSignal._comment: Spencer (later Cory) reviews in the OptimoRoute map UI and says go. Never a timer - silence is not consent. No API signal exists for 'approved' in OptimoRoute.

writeRules._never: Never a continuous sync. Continuous bidirectional reconciliation outside the gate is what scrambled the board on 2026-07-06.
writeRules.lateBookingsDuringReview: NOT written. The plan writes exactly what was approved. New bookings go to the mid-week add queue.

authorityModel._decision: Spencer 2026-08-21: human-driven until we have proven everything works flawlessly.
authorityModel._default: No automation writes to Jobber or OptimoRoute on a timer. A write happens because a person started the run and granted authority for it, and the grant expires on its own. Silence is not consent and neither is a schedule.
authorityModel._standingGrantsWhy: Exactly one, and it is narrow, customer-facing and long-proven. It is the exception that shows the shape of the bar, not a precedent to copy.
authorityModel.routeHorizonExtend: HUMAN_DRIVEN. Chains push-week + optimize-week, which write times back to real customer schedules. Stays cron-disabled; the 3-week horizon is advanced by a person running it, not by a schedule.
authorityModel._promotionBar: PROPOSED, needs Spencer confirmation. Before any chain earns a standing grant it should have run in shadow across a full week with its proposals compared to what a human would have done, produced zero unexplained diffs, and had the watchdog quiet throughout. Recording this so "proven" is a test somebody can pass, not a feeling.

optimoRoute._comment: Known landmines. These matter more now that OR is the human review surface - a ghost stop means someone approves a route containing a customer nobody is visiting.
optimoRoute._balancingWhy: ON_FORCE reassigns stops across drivers, which violates territory ownership during review.
optimoRoute._priorityWhy: OR serves higher-priority orders earlier in the day, which warped routes ~20% (the Kenmore zigzag). Never encode promises as priority.
optimoRoute._ghostWhy: Push/sync can CREATE and UPDATE but cannot RETIRE an order. A cancelled, completed or moved visit leaves its stop behind. 8 ghosts in the week of 08-10 carried 189 min of drive time that was not real.
optimoRoute._reviewHorizonWhy: Spencer 2026-08-21: OptimoRoute is currently planned about a week out and he wants three. A new booking needs a planned day to land on; with a 1-week horizon most new customers are booked past the last planned day and are invisible to anything that reconciles against the plan. Three weeks also covers the arrival-window email cutoff and a normal cadence interval. NOTE the retired route-horizon-extend cron used 19 days — 3 weeks is 21, so that job needs its number changed, not just re-enabling.

operationalGuards.neverPipeLiveWrites: Never pipe a live write script through head or a line-capped sed - closing the pipe SIGPIPEs node mid-write. Redirect to a file and grep the file.
operationalGuards.visitEditAssignedUsersReplaces: The mutation REPLACES the assignee list, it does not append.
operationalGuards.recurringAssignRetryable: visitEditAssignedUsers can fail transiently on recurring visits with 'required to handle future items'. There is no scope argument to supply - it is Jobber-side flakiness. Retry the pass rather than hand-editing.
operationalGuards.cronsOffDuringManualEditing: Any cron that writes to the board must be stopped before a manual editing session, or it treats human moves as drift.

outOfScope: Same-day disruption - sick techs, blown days, weather. Spencer handles these.
Recurring visit generation - stays Jobber's. The engine places visits and adds interim ones.
How techs write notes - separate training track.
OptimoRoute configuration beyond driver work windows.

openQuestions.question: What fraction of visit notes actually carry Latest Activity / Moles Caught / Misses / Next Action, per tech?
openQuestions.why: Determines whether cadence can be driven from structured fields at all. If coverage is poor it is a note-convention fix that must land before any engine — no scheduler can infer what was never written down.

resolvedQuestions.answer: Visit 1 holds the sold day; from visit 2 it settles onto the grid day.
Three weeks (21 days). Currently about one.
Loan is over. Robert Norton owns Federal Way 98003/98023. Confirmed against completed work since the cut: both zips 100% Robert, Thursdays.
Human-driven until proven flawless. No new standing grants.
